title.narrative: Rapid response to provide life-saving support to those affected by Cyclone Chido

description.narrative: Cyclone Chido made landfall on 15 December in Mecúfi district, Cabo Delgado province with winds of up to 165 km/h and heavy rains exceeding 250 mm in 24 hours. The early-season cyclone has caused widespread devastation across northern Mozambique, affecting Cabo Delgado, Nampula, and Niassa provinces. Infrastructure damage is extensive, disrupting roads, energy, and communication networks. Many communities are isolated and have limited or no access to basic services. In Mecúfi and Chiure districts, destruction is nearly total, with few structures still standing.As of December 23, 2024, the INGD reported that 453,971 people were affected by the cyclone across six provinces. The cyclone also caused over 100 deaths. INGD reported that 102,600 houses were destroyed/damaged. Public infrastructure including 52 health facilities and over 1,200 classrooms were also damaged. Women and children account for an estimated 75% of those affected. Many displaced families initially sought refuge in accommodation centres, where conditions were overcrowded and access to basic resources limited. Cabo Delgado province and other heavily affected areas are characterized by high poverty levels and limited access to services, further compounding the humanitarian impact of the cyclone.UNICEF will provide life-saving wash, child protection and integrated health and nutrition programming in Cabo Delgado and Nampula provinces to those hit by the cyclone and who have received minimal support. Responding quickly to the cyclone, UNICEF teams have been working with authorities to restart basic services include health facilities or mobile health networks, establish child friend spaces, and provide both immediate hygiene supplies in accommodation centres as well as support the restarting of water supply services. Fuel to run water supply networks, water trucking and distraction of hygiene supplies remain priorities to ensure populations have access to safe water. Given the damage and loss to health facilities, UNICEF will provide tents to be used as temporary facilities as well as medicines, medical supplies and other equipment to ensure communities have access to health services. Where communities are more remote, UNICEF will support the deployment of integrated mobile brigades. Child Protection activities include MHPSS and case management. Activities will target communities (WASH), women and girls (health), and children and caregivers (CP). UNICEF's implementing partners will include government district line ministries, international and national NGO partners, and contractors for rehabilitation work. The programme will help people recover and build back better (infrastructure) from the cyclone's impact.
